rows.answer:
Adults aged 18 or over can pay up to £20,000 into ISAs in the 2026/27 tax year (6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027). You can split this between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs, innovative finance ISAs and a Lifetime ISA. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Any unused allowance does not carry forward.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The ISA allowance for 2026/27 is £20,000 per adult aged 18 or over. The tax year runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027. You can split the allowance between cash, stocks and shares, innovative finance and Lifetime ISAs. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Unused allowance does not carry forward.

The cash ISA cap of £12,000 for under-65s starts from 6 April 2027, so it doesn't apply in 2026/27. More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The documents I found only cover adults. They say adults aged 18 or over can pay into ISAs, and that a Lifetime ISA can be opened by anyone aged 18 to 39. They don't say whether a 17-year-old can open an ISA with us, so I can't confirm it.

You could ask your adviser, or call the firm directly, to check what is available for her.

You can pay up to £4,000 a year into a Lifetime ISA, which counts towards the £20,000 overall allowance. The government adds a 25% bonus of up to £1,000 a year. A Lifetime ISA can be opened by anyone aged 18 to 39.

Money can be withdrawn without charge in three cases:
- To buy a first home costing £450,000 or less, provided the account has been open for at least 12 months.
- From age 60.
- If you are terminally ill with less than 12 months to live.

Other withdrawals incur a 25% government charge. More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

rows.answer:
At 42 you're too old to open a Lifetime ISA. They can only be opened by people aged 18 to 39.

The ISA guide says the overall ISA allowance is £20,000 in the 2026/27 tax year. It can be split between cash, stocks and shares, and innovative finance ISAs. I can't tell you which option suits you. If you'd like advice on that, I can pass you to an adviser.

More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The changes take effect from 6 April 2027:

- Investors under 65 can pay up to £12,000 into cash ISAs each tax year. The overall £20,000 ISA allowance is unchanged, so the remainder can still go into stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs. Investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit.
- Transfers from stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs into cash ISAs will no longer be permitted.
- A charge will apply to interest paid on cash held inside a stocks and shares or innovative finance ISA.
- Money already in cash ISAs is not affected by the cap.

More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

For advice on what to do with your own ISAs, please speak to an adviser.

The guide says that from 6 April 2027, the amount investors under the age of 65 can pay into cash ISAs each tax year will be capped at £12,000. It also says investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit.

You told me you're 70, and I can't verify that. If it's correct, you're in the 65 and over group. The guide doesn't cover your personal circumstances, so please raise anything specific to you with your adviser.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

rows.answer:
Under HM Revenue & Customs' guidelines, ISA transfers should complete within 30 calendar days. Transfers between cash ISAs should take no more than 15 working days. Moving holdings as they are (in specie) can take longer if fund managers are slow to respond.

The receiving provider starts the transfer. If your holdings are sold first and moved as cash, the proceeds move once the sales settle. That is normally within four working days of dealing. We don't charge for transfers in or out, and we keep you informed through the portal at each stage.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/closing-or-transferring/

Yes. Our stocks and shares ISA is flexible. Money you withdraw during a tax year can be replaced in that same tax year without using more of your allowance.

The documents I found don't give any more detail, such as conditions or exceptions. If you want to check how this applies to your own ISA, please raise it with your adviser. More information is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Yes, in part. A surviving spouse or civil partner is entitled to an additional permitted subscription equal to the value of the deceased's ISAs. This is on top of their own allowance. It applies whether or not they inherit the investments themselves.

Your ISA also stays tax-free as a continuing account of a deceased investor for up to three years while the estate is administered. ISAs form part of your estate for inheritance tax.

The documents don't say what you or your wife should do in your situation. Please raise that with your adviser. More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The pension annual allowance is £60,000. If the total paid into your pensions in a tax year exceeds it, an annual allowance charge is normally due. The total includes employer contributions and the value of any defined benefit accrual.

- **High earners:** the allowance tapers down to a minimum of £10,000.
- **Carry forward:** you can carry forward unused allowance from the previous three tax years. You must have been a member of a registered pension scheme in those years.
- **Money purchase annual allowance:** once you have taken taxable income flexibly from a defined contribution pension, a £10,000 allowance applies to further defined contribution contributions.

More detail is in the pensions guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Up to 25% of a pension can normally be taken tax free. This is subject to the lump sum allowance of £268,275 across all your pensions. Lump sums above the allowance are taxed at your marginal rate.

I can't advise on how much you should take or when. If you want advice on that, I can pass you to an adviser. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

You can draw from a defined contribution pension from age 55. This rises to 57 from 6 April 2028. The options are flexi-access drawdown, buying an annuity, taking lump sums, or a combination. Each has different tax consequences.

When you apply to access a pension, we will refer you to Pension Wise. We will also offer to book a free guidance appointment for you. We won't do this if you have already had one or have received regulated advice.

I can't tell you which option suits you. If you'd like advice on that, I can pass you to an adviser. More detail is on the Pensions guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Yes. If the transfer value is more than £30,000, the law requires you to take appropriate independent advice before the transfer can proceed. The advice must come from a firm with Financial Conduct Authority permission to advise on pension transfers. Fernhill Wealth holds that permission.

The Financial Conduct Authority expects advisers to start from the assumption that a transfer won't be suitable. Fernhill recommends one only where it can show the transfer is clearly in your interest.

The documents don't say what the rules are for transfer values of £30,000 or less.

Based on our pensions guide:

From 6 April 2027, most unused pension funds and death benefits will be included in the value of your estate for inheritance tax. Benefits passing to a spouse or civil partner, or to a registered charity, remain exempt. Dependants' scheme pensions and death-in-service benefits are outside the new rules.

Income tax is separate. If you die before age 75, benefits are normally paid free of income tax, within the lump sum and death benefit allowance of £1,073,100. If you die at or after 75, the recipient pays income tax at their marginal rate.

The guide doesn't say how this applies to your own circumstances. For that, please raise it with your adviser. More detail is in the pensions guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Our standard rates for financial planning are:

- **Full financial plan:** £2,400, plus VAT where it applies. It covers a review of your whole financial position, a written plan with recommendations, and a meeting to go through it.
- **One-off advice on a single topic:** £1,200, plus VAT where it applies. An example is how to use allowances before the end of the tax year.

We are paid by fees agreed with you in advance, not by commission. We confirm all fees in writing in your client agreement and services and costs disclosure before any work starts. You can see the details on our Fees and Charges page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

Ongoing advice costs 0.75% a year of the assets under advice. It's collected monthly from your accounts. It covers your annual review meeting, access to your adviser throughout the year, rebalancing recommendations and the quarterly reports.

More details are on the fees page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/
